incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a vulnerability in Free-for-Teacher accounts to access the platform, then defaced login pages with a ransom message after Instructure declined to pay an earlier extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline for hours, forcing universities including Princeton, UPenn, Duke, Ohio State, and Texas to delay final exams; attackers claim 3.6 TB of student/faculty data including names, emails, student IDs, and private messages. Several universities are reportedly negotiating directly with the gang.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal agencies (via DC-based software contractor)
incidents.vector: Two former employees of a software vendor serving 45+ federal agencies (including the EEOC) used retained access after being fired to write-protect, delete, and destroy government databases.
incidents.impact: Sohaib Akhter convicted of deleting 96 government databases and password trafficking; faces up to 21 years in prison. His twin brother was also implicated. Incident exposes insider-threat risk in cleared-contractor model.

incidents.vector: Malware was discovered on shared lab computers at a Manhattan campus; details on initial infection vector not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Malware was removed and the district is investigating with local police. Disclosed alongside the broader Canvas incident affecting NYC schools nationally.

incidents.victim: Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies (Ivanti EPMM users)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-6973, an improper input validation vulnerability in Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile, added to CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.impact: CISA mandated remediation by federal agencies; Ivanti EPMM is widely deployed for managing employee mobile devices, making compromise an entry point for broader enterprise intrusion.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Buffer overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300) in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal allowed unauthenticated remote code execution as root via crafted packets; attacker injected shellcode into nginx, then deployed open-source EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools previously used by Chinese-nexus actors.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracking limited but ongoing exploitation since April 9 by cluster CL-STA-1132; post-exploit activity included Active Directory enumeration using firewall service accounts and systematic log destruction. Attackers used a SAML flood to fail over to a second device and re-establish access. Patches and mitigations released May 6.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users (government, scientific, manufacturing, retail orgs in Russia, Belarus, Thailand)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised AVB Disc Soft's build/signing infrastructure and shipped backdoored DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate beginning April 8; first-stage backdoor profiles host then selectively deploys QUIC RAT to high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Several thousand systems infected with the first-stage implant, but the QUIC RAT second-stage was deployed to only ~12 carefully chosen victims at government, scientific, manufacturing, and retail organizations. Pattern matches prior Chinese-nexus supply-chain compromises (Notepad++, CCleaner).

incidents.vector: Threat actor gained unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source code repository; details of initial access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no evidence its source-code release or distribution process was affected, but source-code exposure can give attackers a roadmap to evade Trellix's detections downstream. The breach is the latest in a string of cyber-vendor compromises (F5 BIG-IP, Aqua Security/Trivy, Checkmarx KICS) that have material supply-chain risk.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-8302 campaign deploying multiple custom malware families (NetDraft, CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL/SNOWLIGHT, SNOWRUST Rust stager) for long-term access; relies on n-day and zero-day exploitation for initial access, then PowerShell reconnaissance, AD enumeration, and lateral movement using Impacket and WMI.
incidents.impact: Long-term cyberespionage access to government agencies in South America (since late 2024) and southeastern Europe (2025); malware families overlap with multiple Chinese-nexus clusters indicating shared operator tooling.

incidents.victim: Linux systems (millions of hosts on Ubuntu, RHEL, Debian, Amazon Linux, SUSE)
incidents.vector: Local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-31431, 'Copy Fail') in the Linux kernel algif_aead module enables an unprivileged local attacker to overwrite the page cache of setuid binaries (su, sudo, passwd) and escalate to root with a 732-byte deterministic Python script.
incidents.impact: CISA warned of in-the-wild exploitation. Affects all major Linux distributions since 2017, enables container escape, multi-tenant takeover, and CI/CD pipeline compromise. Patching is in progress but adoption will lag for embedded and legacy systems.

incidents.victim: cPanel/WHM hosting providers (~1.5M exposed instances; Guam government among confirmed victims)
incidents.vector: Authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-41940, CVSS 9.8) in cPanel/WHM session loading exploited via mass-scripted attacks. KnownHost confirmed zero-day exploitation as far back as Feb 23; patches released April 28; PoC and detailed write-ups landed within 24 hours of disclosure.
incidents.impact: Censys observed ~15,000 compromised instances within first 24 hours; ~44,000 total cPanel systems compromised per Shadowserver. Attackers deployed Mirai botnet variants and a 'fakestortion' ransomware that wipes sites and appends '.sorry' extensions, demanding $8,000 in Bitcoin. Guam government sites taken offline.

incidents.victim: Organizations in India and Russia (industrial, consulting, retail, transportation)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails impersonating Indian and Russian tax authorities containing archives with a modified Rust-based loader that downloads ValleyRAT and a previously undocumented Python backdoor called ABCDoor.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed 1,600+ malicious messages between January and February 2026. ABCDoor provides multi-monitor screen streaming, remote keyboard/mouse control, clipboard theft, and limited file encryption. Marks Silver Fox's first confirmed expansion into Russian targets.

incidents.victim: DigiCert customers receiving EV code signing certificates
incidents.vector: Social engineering attack against DigiCert tech support staff: attacker posed as a customer and tricked two employees into running a malicious .SCR (Windows screensaver) file. CrowdStrike EDR was misconfigured on one workstation, leaving it disconnected from central management for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attacker stole 27 EV code signing certificates and used them to sign Zhong Stealer malware (linked to Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog/APT-Q-27). All 27 certificates have been revoked; DigiCert says it learned of the abuse only because a third-party researcher tipped them off.

incidents.victim: SAP Cloud Application Programming developer ecosystem (~570K weekly downloads)
incidents.vector: Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm wave compromised four SAP CAP packages (@cap-js/sqlite, @cap-js/postgres, @cap-js/db-service, mbt) starting April 29; preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime then runs an 11.7 MB obfuscated stealer that exfiltrates GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS/Azure/GCP secrets, Kubernetes service-account tokens, Claude/MCP configs, and reads /proc memory of GitHub Actions runners.
incidents.impact: Wave continues a structural pattern from April 22 @bitwarden/cli compromise; uses GitHub commit search API as covert C2 'dead drop' to share stolen tokens, then republishes infected versions of any packages a victim can publish. Targets enterprise developer pipelines and cloud credentials.

incidents.victim: Republic of Moldova — National Health Insurance Agency (CNAM)
incidents.vector: Mysterious intrusion into Moldova's national healthcare insurance database; specific access vector not disclosed by CNAM or Moldova's Cybersecurity Agency.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial information on nearly every adult Moldovan citizen and foreign resident enrolled in the national insurance scheme stolen; CNAM denied initial reports that ~30% of the database was destroyed. Moldovan officials have not ruled out Russian involvement; Russia has threatened Moldova with military intervention amid pro-EU government tensions.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Microsoft Exchange email server at the Cuban diplomatic mission, part of a broader campaign that hit 5,000+ Exchange servers globally.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole email inboxes for Cuban diplomats, reportedly to gain insight into the U.S. naval blockade of Cuba and broader U.S.-Cuba dynamics.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used compromised SSH keys belonging to the CEO of Huge Networks, a Brazilian DDoS-mitigation provider, to operate a Mirai-based botnet of TP-Link Archer AX21 routers vulnerable to CVE-2023-1389; coordinated DNS reflection attacks from the firm's own infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Years-long campaign of massive DDoS attacks against Brazilian ISPs, with attacks limited to Brazilian IP ranges and lasting 10-60 seconds per target. Huge Networks's CEO blames a January 2026 intrusion; KrebsOnSecurity's reporting suggests possible competitor sabotage or self-dealing.

incidents.victim: Vect 2.0 ransomware victims (manufacturing, education, healthcare, technology)
incidents.vector: Vect 2.0 ransomware-as-a-service deployed via TeamPCP supply-chain compromises (Trivy, Checkmarx KICS, LiteLLM, Telnyx) on Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi; partnership announced on BreachForums.
incidents.impact: Check Point research disclosed a fatal cryptographic flaw: for any file >128 KB the malware silently discards three of four ChaCha20 nonces, making files unrecoverable even with a paid decryptor. Effectively functions as a wiper for VM disks, databases, documents, and backups regardless of ransom payment.

incidents.vector: Personal data on 7.5 million Carnival customers, originally stolen earlier in 2026 via voice-phishing/social engineering intrusions, was leaked publicly after extortion negotiations failed.
incidents.impact: 7.5M customer records exposed; part of a broader ShinyHunters campaign also affecting Zara, 7-Eleven, Udemy, and Medtronic in 2026. Adds to the same group's earlier hits on ADT, McGraw Hill, and Rockstar Games.

incidents.vector: World Leaks ransomware/extortion group breached Mediaworks and leaked internal files including content-direction meeting notes.
incidents.impact: Leaked documents revealed Hungarian content directors discussing contacting Moscow for help publishing anti-Ukraine narratives, exposing Hungary-Russia propaganda coordination amid the recent loss of Hungary's pro-Kremlin party in elections. Mediaworks has filed lawsuits against publications that covered the leak.

incidents.victim: Republican Party of Alberta (Canada) — voter database
incidents.vector: A separatist political party in Alberta published a public, searchable database containing voter information; the data was not appropriately access-controlled.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 2.9 million Alberta voters exposed online before the database was taken down following legal action by the provincial election agency.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an admin account, set the delay on admin actions to zero, and executed unauthorized transactions instantly across multiple blockchain integrations.
incidents.impact: $5 million in crypto assets stolen from the platform's cross-chain integration.

incidents.vector: Compromised employee account used to access internal systems containing customer data.
incidents.impact: Customer data stolen; company says the incident is contained and is investigating the scope of stolen data.

incidents.vector: March 2026 cyberattack of unspecified type; details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hasbro delayed publication of Q1 2026 financial results due to ongoing system restoration; the incident caused shipping and invoicing delays and disrupted financial reporting workflows.

incidents.vector: SafePay ransomware group claimed the breach and leaked stolen data online.
incidents.impact: Operational data exfiltrated and posted to the SafePay leak site; impact on production and customers not yet detailed.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-32201, a SharePoint Server spoofing vulnerability that allows attackers to present falsified content/interfaces over a network within trusted SharePoint environments.
incidents.impact: Microsoft confirmed active exploitation when patches were released on Patch Tuesday alongside 167 total fixes including a publicly disclosed Windows Defender flaw ('BlueHammer'). Spoofing in trusted document repositories is a high-quality phishing/social-engineering primitive.

incidents.vector: Sustained DDoS-for-hire attack against Canonical's web infrastructure by the pro-Palestinian 313 Team hacktivist group, peaking at attacks claimed in excess of 3.5 Tbps.
incidents.impact: Multiple Canonical/Ubuntu domains and APIs taken offline for days; users could not install or update Ubuntu. Same group previously took down BlueSky and Mastodon.

incidents.vector: A student used software-defined radio (SDR) and handheld radios to transmit a high-priority 'General Alarm' signal to the rail network's control communications.
incidents.impact: Four trains halted for 48 minutes after emergency braking procedures were triggered. Demonstrates persistent risk from unauthenticated radio-based control signaling on critical transport infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Internal corporate systems breach; details of access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Itron disclosed the breach was discovered April 13 and has been resolved; cyber insurance is expected to cover most costs. Vendor supplies smart-meter and grid-management technology to utilities globally.
